Matching Program","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/19/2026-23616/privacy-act-of-1974-matching-program","summary":"This matching program will support the U.S. Department of Education (ED) and the Department of War (DoW) in meeting the requirements set forth in Section 559(b) of the Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, which requires the Secretary of Education and the Secretary of War to enter into a matching program to identify servicemembers and staff eligible for certain public service loan forgiveness programs. Under this matching program, DoW (source agency) will disclose to the ED, Federal Student Aid (FSA), (recipient agency), information on individuals who, at any time beginning on or after October 1, 2007, were members of the Armed Forces serving on active duty for a period of more than 30 consecutive days or civilian employees of DoW, for the purposes of: (1) identifying whether they made one or more student loan payments eligible to be counted for purposes of the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program under subsection 455(m) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (HEA) and Temporary Expanded PSLF (TEPSLF) program; and (2) without requiring further information from them, certifying the total period of such service or employment for purposes of such program and counting the total number of qualifying payments made by them for purposes of such program during such period. ED will evaluate the information that it receives from DoW to create a count of qualifying payments under PSLF made by covered employees on their respective Title IV Loans (as defined herein). In addition, ED will create customized notifications for covered employees based on the status of their respective Title IV Loans and whether they have already submitted a PSLF and TEPSLF Certification and Application (PSLF form).","publishedAt":"2026-11-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23531","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; In carrying out these activities, NCEE, in collaboration with the National Center for Special Education Research (NCSER), has identified six aspects of IDEA implementation for consideration of evaluation: access; appropriate services and educational outcomes; procedural safeguards; statewide systems, accountability, and flexibility; fiscal and resource effectiveness; and national activities. Through this request for information (RFI), NCEE seeks public input to identify key questions for future evaluation studies.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23034","title":"Committee and Quarterly Board Meetings; Correction","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23034/committee-and-quarterly-board-meetings-correction","summary":"The National Assessment Governing Board (Board) published a notice in the Federal Register announcing the schedule and proposed agenda for its standing committee meetings and quarterly Board meeting on Thursday, November 19, 2026, and Friday, November 20, 2026.
